rows.title: TRUNK-6382/TRUNK-6360: Backport @Transactional/@Cacheable-on-classes-without-interface fix to 2.6.x
rows.excerpt:
## Summary

Backports the fix for **`@Transactional`/`@Cacheable` not working on classes without an interface** (TRUNK-6382, TRUNK-6360) from Core 2.8.0 onto the `2.6.x` maintenance branch.

## Problem

Upgrading the FHIR2 module (2.6.0+) on Platform 2.6.x causes OpenMRS to fail to start with:

```
BeanCreationException: Error creating bean with name 'appFrameworkService' ...
Cannot convert value of type 'com.sun.proxy.$ProxyNNN implementing
org.springframework.aop.SpringProxy, org.springframework.aop.framework.Advised,
org.springframework.cglib.proxy.Factory, org.springframework.core.DecoratingProxy'
to required type 'org.openmrs.module.appframework.repository.AllComponentsState':
no matching editors or conversion strategy found
```

This isn't unique to the App Framework module — we reproduced the same failure pattern against `dataexchange`'s `DataExporter` bean, and it's the same root cause reported for `stockmanagement` in TRUNK-6382.

Reported by our team here: [FHIR2 OMOD Upgrade Fails on OpenMRS Platform 2.6.17 with AllComponentsState Proxy Conversion Error](https://talk.openmrs.org/t/fhir2-omod-upgrade-2-5-0-2-6-0-fails-on-openmrs-platform-2-6-17-with-allcomponentsstate-proxy-conversion-error/49841).

## Root cause

Several modules (App Framework's `AllComponentsState`, `dataexchange`'s `DataExporter`, etc.) declare `@Transactional` on a concrete class with no interface. Before this fix, `@Transactional`/`@Cacheable` annotation processing silently did not apply to any bean that wasn't an `OpenmrsService`, so these beans were never actually proxied — the raw object was injected directly, and everything worked by accident.

Something in FHIR2 2.6.0+'s own bean graph correctly triggers Spring's transactional annotation-driven infrastructure to *actually* attempt to proxy these beans for the first time. Since they have no interface, Spring's default JDK-dynamic-proxy strategy can't produce a valid proxy assignable to the concrete class — hence the `IllegalStateException`.

This exact bug and fix already exist for Core 2.8.0+ (TRUNK-6382, TRUNK-6360), which switches `@Transactional`/`@Cacheable` proxying to CGLIB (class-based) via `<tx:annotation-driven proxy-target-class="true"/>` / `<cache:annotation-driven proxy-target-class="true"/>`, replacing the old `DefaultAdvisorAutoProxyCreator`/`TransactionAttributeSourceAdvisor` pair. rows.title: TRUNK-6768: Remove unused BOM entries and ban SNAPSHOT dependencies in release builds
rows.excerpt:
## Description of what I changed

This PR audits the BOM against actual module usage, removes unused managed entries, and adds a release-build check that fails on SNAPSHOT dependencies.

Changes:

### 1. BOM Audit (`bom/pom.xml`, `web/pom.xml`)

Audited every managed dependency in `bom/pom.xml` against what `api`, `web`, `webapp`, and `liquibase` actually declare or resolve (via `mvn dependency:tree`).

**Removed (confirmed unused anywhere in the module tree):**
- `org.openmrs.liquibase.ext:type-converter` — confirmed unused via dependency:tree across all modules

**Kept, with explanatory comments** (per the ticket's "deliberately provided with a comment" criterion):
- `jaxen` — required transitively by the `liquibase` module for XML changelog XPath support; not declared by `api`/`web`/`webapp`
- `netty-bom` — pins the Netty version pulled in transitively via the AWS SDK S3 client
- `sonar-jacoco-listeners` — used as a listener dependency for the jacoco-maven-plugin / Sonar coverage integration in the root pom.xml, not a direct project dependency

### 2. Release-build check for SNAPSHOT dependencies (`pom.xml`)

Added a `release` Maven profile using the built-in `banDynamicVersions` Enforcer rule, bound to the `validate` phase, which fails the build if any resolved dependency has a SNAPSHOT version, a version range, or a LATEST/RELEASE placeholder.

Tested:
- `mvn validate -pl api` → passes (normal dev builds unaffected)
- `mvn validate -Prelease -pl api` → fails with a precise message naming the offending SNAPSHOT dependency

### 3. What's NOT included, and why

The ticket also asks for milestone (`-M`), alpha, beta, and RC qualifiers to be banned in release builds. I was unable to implement this with `bannedDependencies` (the rule the ticket suggests) or any other built-in Enforcer rule:

- `banDynamicVersions` only covers SNAPSHOT, version ranges, and LATEST/RELEASE — milestone/alpha/beta/RC versions are not "dynamic" by Maven's definition and are explicitly out of scope for this rule.
- `bannedDependencies`' wildcard support only replaces a *whole* segment (groupId, artifactId, or version) or accepts a real Maven version range. It does not support partial substring matching within the version field (e.g. `*-M*`). rows.title: TRUNK-6766: Replace commons-collections 3.2.2 usage with JDK collections
rows.excerpt:
## Description of what I changed

Core no longer uses the pre-generics commons-collections 3 API.

- `CollectionUtils.isEmpty`/`isNotEmpty`/`MapUtils.isEmpty` → `Collection#isEmpty`. Receivers that can be null (method parameters, lazily created locals, `Obs#getGroupMembers(true)`) keep an explicit null guard, so null handling is unchanged at every call site. Receivers that are never null (lazily initialised domain getters, JPA result lists, locals) call `isEmpty()` directly.
- `CollectionUtils.filter` → `List#removeIf`. `AttributeMatcherPredicate` now implements `java.util.function.Predicate<T>` (`evaluate(Object)` becomes `test(T)`), dropping its unchecked cast.
- `PatientIdentifierTypeDefaultComparator`: `ComparatorChain`/`NullComparator` → an equivalent `Comparator` chain (`nullsFirst`/`nullsLast`). The chain is now a static constant, so this `Serializable` comparator no longer holds non-serializable lambdas as instance state.
- `ConceptValidatorChangeSet`: `ListOrderedSet` → `LinkedHashSet`, dropping an `@SuppressWarnings("unchecked")`.
- Tests: `CollectionUtils.disjunction`/`ListUtils.subtract` → `List#removeAll`. Added `AttributeMatcherPredicateTest` and null-ordering coverage for `PatientIdentifierTypeDefaultComparator`.
- Removed the dependency from `api/pom.xml` and the BOM, and excluded it from `commons-validator`. Core only uses validator's `routines` package (`EmailValidator`), which doesn't need it.

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Status |
|---|---|
| No imports of `org.apache.commons.collections` remain | ✅ |
| Unchecked-cast suppressions that existed only for the pre-generics API are removed | ✅ |
| Existing tests pass unchanged; null/empty edge cases covered where semantics change | ✅ (no call site changes null semantics) |
| 3.2.2 absent from every module's dependency tree and the BOM | ⏳ Removed from the BOM. It still arrives through `commons-beanutils`, which goes away with TRUNK-6767 (#6612 ) and TRUNK-6812 (#6616). With all three merged, no module's tree contains it. |

### Notes for reviewers / module authors
- `AttributeMatcherPredicate#evaluate(Object)` is now `test(T)`.
- Modules that relied on the BOM for the commons-collections version will need to declare it themselves.

rows.title: maven(deps): bump org.owasp.encoder:encoder from 1.4.1 to 1.5.0
rows.excerpt:
Bumps [org.owasp.encoder:encoder](https://github.com/OWASP/owasp-java-encoder) from 1.4.1 to 1.5.0.
Release notes

Sourced from org.owasp.encoder:encoder's releases.

OWASP Java Encoder 1.5.0

Version 1.5.0 is available from Maven Central. All nine binary/source/Javadoc JARs, four POMs, and their thirteen signatures were downloaded from Central and verified against the retained signed release files. There is no encoder-esapi:1.5.0 release.

Security and correctness

  • Fixes encoded fragments completing outer HTML or XML parser delimiters across trusted-text boundaries in JavaScript HTML/block, CDATA, and XML-comment contexts. Versions through 1.4.1 are affected. See GHSA-g8p6-7r8f-qrpv.
  • Fixes EncodedWriter close/finalization behavior, exception handling, and overflow-safe array-slice validation.
  • Adds JSON encoding APIs and matching JSP/Jakarta tags and EL functions, plus XML 1.1 bindings.

Compatibility and migration

Public Java APIs remain binary and source compatible with 1.4.1 for the three supported libraries. Java 8 remains the minimum runtime; packaged consumers passed on Java 8, 11, 17, 21, and 25.

The security fixes deliberately change some encoded output:

  • JavaScript HTML/block modes emit additional hexadecimal escapes while preserving the string value. Review byte snapshots, cache keys, signatures, and output-size budgets.
  • CDATA preserves parsed text but can expand to 13 output characters per input character and can change parser event boundaries.
  • XML-comment hyphens become ~ under the documented lossy policy.

The optional ESAPI adapter is retired. Version 1.4.1 is its final published release and is unsupported; migrate to direct Java Encoder APIs. Mixing the 1.4.1 adapter with the 1.5 core is not a supported migration.

See the migration notes,
